title: Market access readiness pack — listing acceptance checklist + copy sketch
content:
Purpose
This is a working readiness pack to get Redwood Inference into cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP). Focus: final acceptance checklist for listings + short copy variants we can A/B test on the storefront. This is a draft — meant to consolidate product, legal, and eng inputs before we convert to the formal vendor submission.

Audience
- Internal: GTM launch lead, partner ops, legal review, engineering contact for merchant SKU mapping.
- External: Marketplace submission reviewers, channel PMs.

High-level goals
1) Ensure listing passes technical and security acceptance on first submission.
2) Provide 2–3 short copy variants and one long-form listing description.
3) Map pricing SKUs and billing language to marketplace-friendly terms.
4) Flag open dependencies (screenshots, support doc links, certs).

Quick TL;DR (for execs)
- Core product angle: "Redwood Inference — predictable, low-latency LLM inference with dev-first APIs and enterprise-grade controls."
- Starter SKU: Hosted API metered by token units; Dedicated = monthly reserved capacity; Private = annual license + support.
- Must attach: SOC2 summary + support SLA PDF, quickstart guide url, and architecture diagram (VPC/private flow).

Acceptance checklist (technical / docs / ops) — must pass before submission
[ ] Marketplace account set up and verified for billing (contact: Priya)
[ ] Finalized listing name (see copy options below)
[ ] Logo & marketing assets: 1024x1024 PNG + 16:9 hero PNG (design owner: Sofia)
[ ] One-line summary (<= 80 chars) finalized
[ ] Long description (<= 2000 chars) proofread and legal-approved
[ ] Feature bullets (5 max) — tied to product capability (hosted, dedicated, private, observability, cost controls)
[ ] Pricing SKUs mapped and approval from finance (see SKU mapping section)
[ ] Support contact and escalation path added to listing
[ ] Security docs attached: SOC2 snapshot, DPA link, KMS/HSM note for private deployment
[ ] Product quickstart URL (docs.redwood.com/marketplace-quickstart) live and accessible
[ ] Technical prerequisites documented for Dedicated & Private (minimum GPU types, network ports, VPC peering notes)
[ ] EULA / license text uploaded (legal)
[ ] Contact person for vendor onboarding (GTM owner + eng POC)
[ ] Test user flow validated: sign-up -> obtain API key -> run sample generate request -> receive response (latency < target)

Notes on technical prereqs (short)
- Dedicated: minimum 4x A10G-equivalent vGPUs recommended for initial SKU, autoscale config must be set to burst mode option.
- Private: provide OVA and Helm chart; include KMS integration guide (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault).
- Hosted: list rate limits, token pricing, and streaming response support.
- Telemetry: describe what data is sent to Redwood for metrics (token counts, latency, error rates) and where to opt-out.

SKU & pricing mapping (draft for finance review)
- Hosted Metered: "Redwood API — Generation (per token)" SKU. Unit = 1k tokens. Intro tier: $0.20 / 1k tokens for first 100M tokens (promotional).
- Embeddings: "Redwood API — Embeddings" (per 1k tokens or per embed call).
- Dedicated Reservation: "Redwood Dedicated — Reserved Pool" (monthly commit, tiered by GPU-equivalent capacity). Reserve 1 unit = 8x A10G-equivalent throughput -> $X/month.
- Private License: "Redwood Private — Core License" (annual, includes support band). Add-ons: premium SLA, on-prem install service.
- Note: Marketplace billing often requires listing fixed-price SKUs; include both metered and fixed monthly bundle options. Finance: confirm SKU granularity to avoid double-billing.

Copy variants (A/B test candidates)
One-liners (<= 80 chars)
A) "High-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and cost control."
B) "Ship LLM features faster: low-latency inference, unified ops across clouds."
C) "Production-ready inference — hosted, dedicated, or private deployments."

Short description (<= 300 chars)
Variant 1:
Redwood Inference provides a developer-first platform for serving large language models with predictable latency and clear unit economics. Choose hosted API for fast integration, Dedicated for committed throughput, or Private for regulated workloads. Integrated observability and rollout controls reduce risk in production.

Variant 2:
A unified runtime for running LLMs at scale. Get streaming responses, function/tool calling, and cost-saving batching & caching out of the box. Enterprise features include VPC-private control plane, KMS integrations, and SLA-backed Dedicated capacity.

Long description (storefront friendly, ~900 chars)
Redwood Inference helps engineering teams deliver LLM features reliably and efficiently across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Our GPU-optimized serving runtime applies attention optimizations, continuous batching, and KV cache management to minimize cost while keeping latency predictable. Ship quickly with a simple REST/SDK interface, built-in streaming and tool-calling, and a curated model catalog. For enterprise customers, Redwood Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and SLAs; Redwood Private provides a customer-controlled plane for regulated workloads. The Redwood Console gives token-level cost visibility, per-route dashboards, and rollout tools (canary/A-B). Whether you need low-touch hosted APIs or fully private deployments, Redwood makes inference operationally simple and economical.

Feature bullets (storefront)
- Low-latency, high-throughput LLM serving across clouds
- Hosted API, Reserved Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments
- Transparent token-level cost and latency insights
- Automatic batching, prefix caching, and quantization recommendations
- Canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback

Marketplace QA & validation steps (engineering)
1) Smoke test: deploy a listing test account, run the quickstart flow and capture screenshots of the successful token generation request and Console route dashboard. (Owner: Marco)
2) Performance claim validation: capture 95th percentile latency for a 512-token generate call for the default hosted model and attach CSV. (Owner: Eng-Perf team)
3) Security attestation: upload SOC2 summary PDF and provide DPA link. Confirm artifact hash. (Owner: Legal)
4) Billing mapping test: validate that marketplace invoice lines map to internal billing signals for both metered and bundle SKUs. (Owner: Finance)

Creative/asset notes
- Screenshots: Console route latency graph, per-route cost breakdown, rollout canary UI, quickstart code sample. Use blurred customer data.
- Video (optional): 90s product tour — highlights hosting modes and Console.
- SEO keywords: LLM inference, inference platform, low-latency LLM, model serving, dedicated GPU pools

Open questions / blockers
- Legal: Are there any marketplace-specific restrictions on metered per-token pricing? (action: Priya to confirm)
- Eng: Need final Dedicated minimum capacity and SKU names for submission. (action: Marco)
- Security: Confirm whether SOC2 type 2 is required or SOC2 summary acceptable for initial listing. (action: Liam)
- Product: Decide which tagline to A/B test first. (action: Ayesha)

Next steps (this week)
- Consolidate final copy and brand assets (Sofia) — due EOD Tue
- Finance sign-off on SKU mapping (Priya) — due Wed
- Legal to upload DPA and EULA to vendor portal (Liam) — due Thu
- Run smoke test and collect screenshots (Marco) — due Fri

Appendix: quick links
- Quickstart docs: https://docs.redwood.com/marketplace-quickstart
- Architecture diagram (draft): https://drive.redwood/arch/redwood-marketplace-arch-v2.png
- Related tickets: JIRA-MLIST-78 (SKU mapping), JIRA-MLIST-81 (security artifacts), CONFLUENCE-1234 (listing standards)

Rough notes / brainstorm (keep under working area)
- Consider a fixed-monthly "developer pack" bundle for marketplaces that don't support fine-grained metering — 100k tokens included + overage price.
- Possibly include an "experimental" free tier listing that gives 10k tokens to try streaming for devs (promotional).
- For Private: highlight professional services for install and data residency reassurance.

END — leave comments inline.
